reused_why: the runs that carry over as their own 16K run, listed as `reused` so driver.py --dry-run counts them as not played. A run whose prompt never passed 16,384 before its final call would behave the same at 16,384: the trigger reads the last agent call's exact prompt_tokens and compacts before the next call, so its calls and record would be the same up to sampling. Each lists its counted record's file and run dir in the 32K set's folder (repo-relative), and prompt_before_final_call (the largest agent turn prompt before the final one). 5 carry over as failures (`failed`: end, error and tries): their 32K run failed on every try under the rerun rule and never passed 16,384 before its final call. They are reported as failed and left out of the measures, as at 32K, not counted as finished runs. A failed run whose prompt passed 16,384 is rerun here like any other

stop_at.counted: Jev input tokens summed over every launch of this step

reruns: a run that fails or times out (end error, overflow, crash or timeout, or a Jev error marked rerun) is played again, up to four tries, and the last play stands. A run that fails on every try is reported as failed and left out of every measure, with its pairs. A run that reaches the turn limit (max turns) is a finished run and is kept

failed_32k.why: six 32K runs failed on every try (every one a vLLM 400: the model's tool call had an empty function name). Each carries into the 16K set as a failure if its prompt never passed 16,384 before its final call, with `failed` (end, error, tries) on its `reused` entry, so the analysis leaves it out of the measures and lists it as failed, as it does at 32K. A failed run whose prompt passed 16,384 is rerun here like any other. None is dropped and none counts as a finished run
